Summary: The command: Burn incense morning and evening (Exodus 30:7). Aaron burned sweet incense on the golden altar every morning when he dressed the lamps, and every evening when he lit them.
Commandment: Burn incense morning and evening, as prescribed in Exodus 30:7.
Application: This row narrows the parent group command to this one mitzvah. The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. Hebrews teaches the earthly tabernacle was a copy of the heavenly one, and Christ now serves as high priest in the true tabernacle.
Purpose: To give Israel a mediated approach to God through the tabernacle pattern (Exodus 25:40). Hebrews teaches the earthly copy gave way to Christ's priesthood in the true tabernacle (Hebrews 8:1-6).
Function: Sweet incense rose from the golden altar every morning and every evening, and that daily rhythm is what makes this ceremonial: a rite of continual worship. Its goal was to keep prayer and offering ascending before God without a break, morning when the lamps were dressed and evening when they were lit. It did not address a particular evil; its work was worship, not restraint. The smoke was the visible sign of a people whose approach to God never stopped.
